deck.title: Structure of Nucleic Acids & Replication of DNA

front_blocks.md: Define **nucleotide**.

back_blocks.md: A **nucleotide** is made of a **phosphate group**, a **pentose sugar** and a **nitrogenous base**.

back_blocks.md: A **phosphate group**
A **pentose sugar**
A **nitrogenous base**

front_blocks.md: Describe the structure of **ATP**.

back_blocks.md: **ATP** is a **phosphorylated nucleotide**.
It consists of the base **adenine**, the pentose sugar **ribose** and **three phosphate groups**.

cards.front_md: Describe the structure of **ATP**.
cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: Which two bases are **purines**?

back_blocks.md: **Adenine** and **guanine** are purines, and they have a **double ring** structure.

cards.front_md: Which two bases are **purines**?
cards.back_md: **Adenine** and **guanine** are purines, and they have a **double ring** structure.

front_blocks.md: Which three bases are **pyrimidines**?

back_blocks.md: **Cytosine**, **thymine** and **uracil** are pyrimidines, and they have a **single ring** structure.

cards.front_md: Which three bases are **pyrimidines**?

Thymine and uracil are both purines.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

front_blocks.md: What does it mean that the two DNA strands are **antiparallel**?

back_blocks.md: The two strands run in **opposite directions**.
One runs **5' to 3'** and the other runs **3' to 5'**.

cards.front_md: What does it mean that the two DNA strands are **antiparallel**?
cards.back_md:
The two strands run in **opposite directions**.

One runs **5' to 3'** and the other runs **3' to 5'**.

front_blocks.md: What are the **complementary base pairing** rules in DNA?

back_blocks.md: **Adenine (A)** pairs with **thymine (T)**.
**Cytosine (C)** pairs with **guanine (G)**.

cards.front_md: What are the **complementary base pairing** rules in DNA?
cards.back_md:
**Adenine (A)** pairs with **thymine (T)**.

**Cytosine (C)** pairs with **guanine (G)**.

front_blocks.md: How does the **hydrogen bonding** differ between C–G and A–T base pairs?

back_blocks.md: **C–G** pairs are joined by **three hydrogen bonds**.
**A–T** pairs are joined by **two hydrogen bonds**.

cards.front_md: How does the **hydrogen bonding** differ between C–G and A–T base pairs?
cards.back_md:
**C–G** pairs are joined by **three hydrogen bonds**.

**A–T** pairs are joined by **two hydrogen bonds**.

front_blocks.md: Which bonds link the nucleotides along a single DNA strand?

back_blocks.md: **Phosphodiester bonds** link adjacent nucleotides, joining the **phosphate** of one to the **sugar** of the next.

cards.front_md: Which bonds link the nucleotides along a single DNA strand?
cards.back_md: **Phosphodiester bonds** link adjacent nucleotides, joining the **phosphate** of one to the **sugar** of the next.

C–G base pairs are held together by two hydrogen bonds.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
C–G pairs are held by **three** hydrogen bonds; A–T pairs are held by two.

front_blocks.md: What is **semi-conservative replication**?

back_blocks.md: DNA replication in which each new DNA molecule contains **one original (template) strand** and **one newly synthesised strand**.

cards.front_md: What is **semi-conservative replication**?
cards.back_md: DNA replication in which each new DNA molecule contains **one original (template) strand** and **one newly synthesised strand**.

front_blocks.md: During which stage of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?

back_blocks.md: The **S phase** (synthesis phase) of interphase.

cards.front_md: During which stage of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?
cards.back_md: The **S phase** (synthesis phase) of interphase.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of **DNA polymerase** in replication?

back_blocks.md: It catalyses the addition of new nucleotides to the growing strand by **complementary base pairing**.
It can only add nucleotides in the **5' to 3'** direction.

cards.front_md: What is the role of **DNA polymerase** in replication?
cards.back_md:
It catalyses the addition of new nucleotides to the growing strand by **complementary base pairing**.

It can only add nucleotides in the **5' to 3'** direction.

front_blocks.md: What is the role of **DNA ligase** in replication?

back_blocks.md: It **joins** the fragments of the **lagging strand** together by forming bonds in the sugar–phosphate backbone.

cards.front_md: What is the role of **DNA ligase** in replication?
cards.back_md: It **joins** the fragments of the **lagging strand** together by forming bonds in the sugar–phosphate backbone.

front_blocks.md: Why is the **leading strand** made continuously but the **lagging strand** in fragments?

back_blocks.md: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides in the **5' to 3'** direction.
The **leading strand** is synthesised continuously towards the replication fork.
The **lagging strand** is synthesised in short fragments away from the fork.

cards.front_md: Why is the **leading strand** made continuously but the **lagging strand** in fragments?
cards.back_md:
DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides in the **5' to 3'** direction.

The **leading strand** is synthesised continuously towards the replication fork.

The **lagging strand** is synthesised in short fragments away from the fork.

back_blocks.md: Replication is described as **semi-conservative** because each new molecule keeps one original strand.

front_blocks.md: Give **three differences** between an RNA molecule and a DNA molecule.

back_blocks.md: RNA is **single-stranded**; DNA is double-stranded.
RNA contains the sugar **ribose**; DNA contains deoxyribose.
RNA contains the base **uracil**; DNA contains thymine.

cards.front_md: Give **three differences** between an RNA molecule and a DNA molecule.
cards.back_md:
RNA is **single-stranded**; DNA is double-stranded.

RNA contains the sugar **ribose**; DNA contains deoxyribose.

RNA contains the base **uracil**; DNA contains thymine.

front_blocks.md: What is **mRNA (messenger RNA)**?

back_blocks.md: A **single-stranded** RNA molecule that carries a copy of the genetic code from the **DNA** to the **ribosomes**.
